newsitem.title: MEXICO: Cemex sees higher Q2 Mexico sales vols.
newsitem.headline: Cemex sees higher Q2 Mexico sales vols.

text.p: Mexico-based cement giant Cemex SA has adjusted upwards its second quarter national sales volumes predictions given strong results between January and May, a Cemex director told Reuters Friday.
"Accumulated to May, we have 16 percent growth in national cement sales (over the same period in 1996)," the director said, asking to remain anonymous.
The director said Cemex expected second quarter domestic sales volume to increase by 20 percent over the same April-June period last year when volume sold reached 3.036 million tonnes.

"The outlook we have is that we will close the year with around 10 percent (national sales volume) growth, between 10 and eight percent, against the previous outlooks for growth of between five and six percent," he added.
In 1996, Cemex sold 13.223 million tonnes of cement product in Mexico. The 18 national plants contributed to 43 percent of total group revenues.

Domestic sales between January and March were 5.7 million tonnes, the director said, adding that meant Cemex's national market share in the period was 59 percent of a national consumption figure of 9.7 million tonnes.
On price, the director said there had been little variation in the first half compared with last year's like period.
"Prices are more or less the same...or a little above. Increases have been slow, but the outlook is that they continue going upwards," he added.

Cemex's average price objective for 1997 is between $85-$86 per tonne, the director added. Analysts have calculated in the first quarter of 1997, Cemex achieved a average national price of $78-$79 per tonne. ((-- Daniel Perez-Whitaker, Monterrey bureau +528 345-7617))
